consensus_summary: Barley lacks one fully settled meaning but clusters around two intertwined associations: the humble/cheap grain of the poor (divine provision through lowly means) and the early/Passover-season firstfruits grain whose wave sheaf typifies Christ’s resurrection.
book_summary: Barley is the firstfruits grain—humble, reaped in spring, and presented before the LORD—whose waved sheaf points to Christ risen as the firstfruits.
consensus_core_identification: humble firstfruits grain linked to lowly provision and/or Christ’s resurrection
book_core_identification: humble firstfruits grain whose waved sheaf points to Christ risen as firstfruits
rationale: Both reduce to the same dual core (humble early grain + firstfruits/resurrection typology). The book simply states the pair concisely; consensus responses already treat the two threads as primary or closely combined and list the identical supporting texts. No referent is replaced, narrowed, or broadened.
strongest_objection: Some consensus strands rank humility/provision ahead of firstfruits typology or treat the latter as only a minority reading, yet both strands remain present and non-contradictory.
